issue: PMAT-225 (forjar#506) — nothing named the release a merged ticket would ship in and nothing measured whether the newest tag was old: docs/roadmaps/releases.yaml now declares the release goals in the paiml-implement goal shape (cadence_days, floors, one row per tag, the open goal), every roadmap row a tag's window names carries release:<tag> and every ticket merged since the newest tag carries release:<next.tag>, gate T (scripts/dogfood/tagged.sh) re-derives every row from git and GitHub and is red wherever the declared and the measured disagree or the cut is overdue, scripts/release-goal.sh is the status line and the textual pen, and a daily workflow keeps one issue open while red. Gate A resolves a PR's first ticket id against the roadmap through the same rule (an alias label for a misnamed branch, never a skip).

quorum.kill_rule: the design was grilled before a line was written and the finished diff was judged by three sandboxed lanes twice with the base pinned; a lane could fail the whole diff on one refuted claim, every lane claim was re-run by the orchestrator before it counted, and a round that refuted anything was followed by a fix commit and another round
quorum.rounds: one --mode plan lane on the design (do-not-implement-as-written, seven findings, three changed the design), three --mode plan lanes on the diff at db298604 (3/3 FAIL on two material findings, lane-reduce not agreed), the fix commit ca3f8d70, three --mode plan lanes on it (3/3 PASS, lane-reduce agreed, zero dissent), one --mode plan lane for the CRUX survey, then the orchestrator's reruns and the workspace gate
refuted_claims: C7 as first worded: every ledger row equals `release-goal.sh window TAG`'s output — refuted by round 1 lane 1: the tool omitted the dogfood: and crux: keys the rows for v1.26.0 and v1.27.0 carry, so the text was not the same. Fixed at ca3f8d70: window prints the keys from dogfood_floor on and cut no longer appends them; all five rows are byte-identical to the tool's output (minus its comment lines), re-derived by diff by two round-2 lanes and the orchestrator

R6 as a hunt: the resolver's refusal of an alias declared by two rows (`names none`) was reachable and untested — found by all three round-1 lanes. Fixed at ca3f8d70: tests/falsification_dogfood_harness_and_quorum.rs::gate_a_an_alias_declared_by_two_rows_names_no_owner_and_is_red, red naming both rows

falsification.test: thirteen fixture cases over temp repositories with a bare origin, annotated tags and a stub gh driving the real gate and tool: the green ledger passes and counts; a declared window that disagrees with GitHub, a merged ticket without the next label, a shipped ticket without its label, a ticket claiming a release it was not in, a row naming a tag origin lacks, a due instant one second off, an overdue cut, a version no goal names, a release at the dogfood floor without its receipt, a stray id in a tagged window, and a gh that cannot answer are each red by name; the cut flow books a tag, moves the goal that missed, labels the open window and turns the gate green
falsification.reverted: the gate absent (main): every case panics at `the gate under test must exist`; gate A's two new cases against main's scripts/dogfood/harness.sh and lib/window.sh (stashed): 0 passed, 2 failed — the misnamed branch is red for the receipt it lacks, not for the stray id, and the alias resolves nothing
falsification.observed_failure: docs/audits/logs/PMAT-225-gate-T-mutant.log: the registered mutation (86400 -> 86401) prints `GATE T FAIL next.due is declared 2026-09-10T22:10:01Z … puts the due instant at 2026-09-10T22:10:03Z — the declared goal and the derived one disagree` and exits 1 on the real ledger; docs/audits/logs/PMAT-225-gate-tests.log: 12 + 1 + 19 + 5 + 4 + 9 passed on ca3f8d70
falsification.still_green_when_reverted: the sixteen pre-existing gate A and E cases, which prove the shared window refactor changed neither gate

crux.verdict: accept(a cadence declared in one committed file and measured by a bot — Node.js's release schedule JSON, Kubernetes's sig-release schedule, Rust's forge calendar; a label as the per-change link — Kubernetes kind/ and release-note labels, Rust relnotes, Node.js semver labels; tag containment as the ground truth every changelog generator reads) and reject(an exact-second due instant where every surveyed cadence is day- or week-granular; a repository-wide red on a late release where the surveyed systems red the individual unlabelled change and hold the release itself in a freeze; a human label reconciled against tag containment, which none of them do — forjar keeps the reconciliation because its labels are DERIVED from the window, never assigned by hand)
